clue.text: Make out fabulous stores close to retail chain

indicators.note: stores means the two words hold another letter within them

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, to make out
ace is slang for excellent or fabulous

indicators.note: close to points to the final letter of the word retail

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talking their way through a story about a shop chain's stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of beads or links worn round the neck is a chain of jewellery.

clue.text: Trouble in new language? You should have it at your fingertips

definitions.text: You should have it at your fingertips

indicators.note: in places the word for trouble inside the other pieces

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with a new language is told they should know it inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at your fingertips' suggests knowing something by heart, but here it is literally on the fingernails.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish for the nails is applied to the tips of the fingers.

clue.text: Like a joiner's debut in carpentry work — value it poorly

indicators.note: the debut in a word is its first letter

parts.note: OP, opus, is a work

indicators.note: poorly means the letters are in a bad state and rearranged

explanation.surface: A carpenter's first piece of work is valued low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but in grammar a copulative word joins, as a conjunction or linking verb does.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a copulative is a joining word, such as and, or a linking verb.

clue.text: Throwing up portion of crisps ill-advisedly makes sinner less fat?

indicators.note: Throwing up says the hidden letters are read backwards
portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone vomits after unwisely eating crisps, and wonders if that helps them slim.
explanation.walkthrough: A speaker with this impediment says 'sinner' as 'thinner', so the definition is a playful example; in a down answer 'Throwing up' reads it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronouncing an s as th turns the word sinner into thinner, which is less fat.

clue.text: Sign of Labour and Tory battles about heads of Treasury

indicators.note: about means the political words go around the letters from the department

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, CON for short
actions are battles or engagements

indicators.note: heads of takes the opening letters of the word Treasury

explanation.surface: A political report on the two main parties fighting over Treasury chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular tightenings of the womb are the sign that childbirth has begun.

clue.text: Hang on! It's a very subdued finale

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for playing very quietly
a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A conductor urges the orchestra to wait for the hushed closing bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach something to the end of a document is to hang it on, as an appendix.

clue.text: Fleet Street heart-throb gets closer

parts.note: Fleet Street in London was the home of the national newspapers, so stands for the press
a stud is an attractive man, a heart-throb

explanation.surface: A newspaper pin-up moves in on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A popper or snap fastener is something that closes a garment.

clue.text: Pencil case, mirror, pens, ruler

indicators.note: pens means encloses: the words case and mirror hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A list of the contents of a school pencil case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pencil case' is part of the picture; the letters come from case and mirror, which pen the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Action in 2-D

indicators.note: in two dimensions suggests a word that reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act, something done.

clue.text: Grand confession from show-off

definitions.meaning: grand in the sense of impressive and stately
a poser admitting what they are doing would say 'I am posing', run together as one word

explanation.definitionFit: Something imposing is impressive in size or bearing, which is grand; the second sense is the phrase I'm posing.

clue.text: Notice skirts twirling in opener from Lady Gaga

indicators.note: skirts means the word for notice goes round the outside of the other letters

parts.note: to notice is to see

indicators.note: twirling turns the little word in round so it reads backwards
the opener from a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fan spots a twirling skirt during the first number of a Lady Gaga concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Gaga' looks like one name, but Gaga, meaning senile, is the definition and Lady only supplies its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is slang for doddery and losing one's faculties in old age.

clue.text: Reformed human sin with Pope Victor's tactics

indicators.note: Reformed means the letters are remade into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reformed sinner joins the pontiff in a victory strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of gaining an advantage over others is the method by which a winner prevails.

clue.text: Winning back Liberals, virtuous type calls to exert influence

indicators.note: back says the word for winning is read in reverse

parts.note: a team that is ahead or winning is up
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, so two give LL
ST, saint, is the virtuous type
to call on the telephone is to ring

explanation.surface: A political campaigner wins Liberal voters back with a saintly figure phoning round.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull strings is an idiom for using one's connections to get things done, exerting influence.

clue.text: Father becoming "pater" in old German territory?

parts.note: Pa is a word for father
pater is the Latin for father, so turning father into it is latinate

explanation.surface: A dad being called by the old school word for father in a German region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palatinate was a historic territory of the Holy Roman Empire in western Germany.

clue.text: Troubled developer requires a financial hand-out to be on track

parts.note: the dole is unemployment benefit, a financial hand-out
scent is the trail a hound tracks

explanation.surface: A troubled property developer needs a state handout to stay on course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developer' suggests property, but is someone still growing; British 'dole' is unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is still developing and often troubled, a playful description.

clue.text: Free toy? About time!

indicators.note: About means the toy's name goes around the abbreviation for time

parts.note: Lego is a construction toy of plastic bricks

explanation.surface: A child, kept waiting, finally gets given a free toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to release it, to set it free.

clue.text: Nothing's stopping complete poet getting beyond the limits of his craft?

definitions.text: beyond the limits of his craft

parts.note: over means finished, complete

indicators.note: stopping means the letter plugs a gap in the word for poet

parts.note: a bard is a poet
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet goes beyond the limits of his art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a skill, but it is a boat; going over the side is beyond its limits.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over the side of a ship takes you outside the bounds of the vessel.

clue.text: For this, seek knave? King or queen included, too

parts.note: to court someone is to seek their favour or hand
a card is an old word for a rogue or knave

explanation.surface: A card player asks what kind of card a jack belongs to, noting kings and queens are in the same set.
explanation.walkthrough: The jack, or knave, is itself a court card, so 'For this, seek knave?' works as a hint as well as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture cards of a pack are king, queen and jack, so the kings and queens are included in this class.

clue.text: Anti-capitalist movement thus is ousting North America from Asian country

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: ousting says one piece pushes out another and takes its place in the country's name

parts.note: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia
NA is the abbreviation for North America
is is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sentence about a communist movement being expelled from an Asian country by Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine and practice of the Soviet system was a communist, anti-capitalist movement.

clue.text: Way of speaking Latin pupil rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: a ward is a minor under a guardian's care, a pupil in old legal use

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is turned down by his Latin class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' as a ward is the old Scottish legal sense of a minor in guardianship.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, drawn-out manner of speech.

clue.text: Crazy family's slippers seen on these?

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin means family, and the possessive gives an s

explanation.surface: A mad family's footwear is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippers' looks like footwear; the peels are things people slip on, so slippers in a comic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Peels dropped on the ground are the classic comic cause of people losing their footing.

clue.text: Unqualified, drunken fortune-teller

indicators.note: drunken suggests slurring, so the opening s sound is said as sh

parts.note: a seer foretells the future

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant without credentials who is also drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means absolute or utter, not qualified by anything.

clue.text: Turned up source of light whimper

indicators.note: turned up says the word reads bottom to top in this down answer

parts.note: a bulb is a source of light

explanation.surface: A dimmer switch is turned up and a light whimpers.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is to cry or snivel, a whimper.

clue.text: Terribly sweet with no end of mawkishness

definitions.text: Terribly sweet with no end of mawkishness

indicators.note: Terribly means the letters are rearranged once the extra one is taken away
end of picks the final letter of mawkishness

explanation.surface: A dessert so sickly that it lacks even the final touch of mawkishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sentimental, cloyingly sweet.

clue.text: Boozer gaining weight around middle — such a product could help!

indicators.note: gaining means the pub takes in the extra letter, here at its centre

parts.note: a boozer is a pub, and the local is your nearby pub

explanation.surface: A drinker putting on a belly might be helped by diet products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around middle' places the W at the centre of LOCAL; a British 'local' is the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-calorie foods are sold to help people lose weight gained around the waist.

clue.text: One's tied in second till leader drops out of position

parts.note: to till soil is to hoe it

indicators.note: leader drops out of means the first letter of the word for position is removed

parts.note: a place is a position

explanation.surface: Someone loses their place in a queue at the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' looks like a cash register but is the verb for working soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A lace for a shoe is a thing that gets tied, defined by what is done to it.

clue.text: Woman's rear clad in lingerie

indicators.note: clad in means the word for rear is wrapped by the garment

parts.note: a bra is a piece of lingerie
the rear is the end

explanation.surface: A woman's bottom dressed in underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: It has a laxative effect in repeat runs

indicators.note: runs signals the letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A medicine that sends you repeatedly to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like part of the laxative picture, diarrhoea, but it is the anagram signal for IN REPEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a mild purgative medicine that loosens the bowels.
